title_en: Wonders of Chinese Engineering (12/20): The Canton Tower
note_en: 着 after a verb describes an ongoing state rather than a one-time action: 塔的外部由一层镂空的钢结构网格包裹着 "the outside of the tower is wrapped in a lattice of open steel mesh." English uses a passive participle ("is wrapped"), but Chinese keeps the active verb 包裹 and adds 着 to show the wrapping stays in place; the text uses it again in 安装着 "has (equipment) installed" and 保持着 "held (the record)."
